comments.text: GREETINGS EVERYONE! Well, I've finally done it. Grabbed so many jackets that I had to cut the video into pieces because I didn't want to carry a ~40lb bag, a camera bag, and a tripod on a few-mile hike. I'm using this opportunity + the fact that I'm posting a waxed jacket video in mid-May to reflect and realize the reason I post so infrequently may be because the videos have become FAR too large. All that being said -- I'll be shrinking them down a tad so I can post more! I CAN DO IT! I BELIEVE IN MYSELF! Okay, pce.

It is actually really easy to make your own waxed shirt or jacket. Mix Gulf wax and mineral oil in a 50/50 ratio. Melt, mix, and apply liberally with a sacrificial paint brush. Then use a cheap iron to go over it and make sure the penetration is even. Let it cool and brush off any excess wax.

Loving your stuff. As an Englishman of a certain vintage, some comment on Barbour. I have had one for over 25 years, but I am never sure why I got it. Growing up, the Barbour was the uniform a particular kind of upper class twit, or wannabe upper class twit, who brayed loudly in public and drove Range Rovers through city centres for an off-road experience. And then French BCBG-types would wear them in immaculate pristine condition around Paris. I wanted to scream! Fortunately, I overcame this cos play country-man environment, took out a second mortgage and bought my Barbour and absolutely knackered it in the outdoors, where it is meant to live and play...It now sits proudly in the boot of my car, weathered, withered, repaired (or rather bodged) by myself, with rips in the pockets and wax re-applied annually. Frankly I could never afford to replace it.
